text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High KV cache eviction rate + continuous-batching latency spike detected for prod-cluster-3. Severity: P1.

alyssa (oncall): seeing a huge uptick in cache put/edit churn, tail latency for short-gen requests > 2s. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/obs/kv-evict?range=5m :boom:

prateek (eng-runtime): ack. pulling traces now. likely related to the new batching policy that rolled ~15m ago.

maria (sre): oncall stepping in — can someone post the deploy/change id? ops-bridge-bot, roll history?

ops-bridge-bot: rollout@deploys: model-runtime: batch-policy-v3 deployed to prod-cluster-3 at 2734567780 by ci-bot.

alyssa (oncall): ok that matches. reverting batch-policy-v3 -> batch-policy-v2 now. running: 
```bash
kubectl -n runtime set configmap batch-config batch-policy=v2 --record
kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-workers -n runtime
```

prateek (eng-runtime): copying logs, but quick note: we've observed KV prefix-key churn where prompt-hash keys are getting regenerated due to tokenizer mapping drift. That + aggressive batching seems to amplify cache write amplification.

dan (customer-ops): any customer-facing impact yet? I'm seeing error-rate bump for conversational endpoints for three enterprise customers. they reported 500s and slow responses ~3m ago.

alyssa (oncall): customer impact: medium→high. adding customer list to thread. Dan, pls flag customers and we will start notifications.

dan (customer-ops): affected: acme-payments, travelbuddy, docwrite-inc. I started templated status notifications to acme-payments.

prateek (eng-runtime): revert completed. rolling restart finished for runtime-workers on cluster-3. latency trending down but KV evictions still elevated in some pods. suspect prefix cache invalidations not fully stabilized because some workers still have stale tokenizer maps.

maria (sre): we should throttle continuous batching to reduce write amplification while we fix tokenizer mismatch. Alyssa — can you flip the dynamic config to safer defaults?

alyssa (oncall): doing that now. changing continuous_batch.window_ms from 30 -> 10 and continuous_batch.max_batch_tokens 4096 -> 2048. Exec: 
```json
{
  "continuous_batch": {"window_ms": 10, "max_batch_tokens": 2048, "kv_write_back": "async"}
}
```
config apply ID: cfg-2734567905

ops-bridge-bot: config apply succeeded (cfg-2734567905).

prateek (eng-runtime): after throttle: per-pod KV writes down ~60%, tail latency improving, but we still see prompt-key regen logs: 
```
WARN prompt_prefix.py: token_map_mismatch detected lambda=0.23 keys_changed=1200
```
This indicates tokenizer mapping upgrade between model variants + cached prefix fingerprinting mismatch. Need a hotfix: make prompthashing tolerant (backwards-compatible) and add a migration to rehash stable prefixes.

maria (sre): agreed. for immediate mitigation, add a short-lived TTL increase for prefix keys to avoid cascading refills: set kv.prefix_ttl from 60 -> 600s. Alyssa can you apply?

alyssa (oncall): applied kv.prefix_ttl=600s (cfg-2734567930). Observability: prefix cache fill rate dropping.

dan (customer-ops): pinged acme-payments with update: "we've identified a temporary service degradation related to internal cache churn; mitigation in progress; next update in 20m."

prateek (eng-runtime): pushing a quick patch to hashing to accept tokenizer remaps: 
```python
# short-term tolerant hash: include tokenizer version fallback
def prompt_fingerprint(prefix_tokens, tokenizer_version):
    try:
        return stable_hash(prefix_tokens, tokenizer_version)
    except TokenMismatchError:
        return stable_hash(prefix_tokens, fallback_tokenizer_version)
```
will open PR and ship a fast patch to runtime image. need approval for canary deploy to prod-cluster-3 (1% traffic).

maria (sre): approve canary. coordinate with oncall for rollout window.

alyssa (oncall): scheduling canary now. oncall watch: @prateek pls monitor kv evictions and per-route error rates.

ops-bridge-bot: canary rollout started (image: runtime:patch-prompthash-273456). canary -> 1% pods.

prateek (eng-runtime): canary logs show prompthash fallback triggered ~30x, but no new evictions or latency spikes in canary. good signal.

alyssa (oncall): increasing canary to 10% after 5m stable.

ops-bridge-bot: canary increased to 10%.

dan (customer-ops): acme-payments reports latency back to normal for most calls, a few retries still needed.

prateek (eng-runtime): pushing full rollout to cluster-3.

ops-bridge-bot: rollout to prod-cluster-3 completed at 2734568010.

alyssa (oncall): monitoring — KV evictions and prefix cache fill look back to baseline over last 3m. customer error rates trending down.

maria (sre): great. immediate actions summary: revert batching policy, throttle continuous batching, increase prefix TTL, patch tolerant prompt hashing, staged rollout.

prateek (eng-runtime): follow-up (postmortem items):
- root cause: tokenizer version drift + stricter batch policy => increased prefix rekey churn -> KV write amplification -> latency cliff under tail.
- short-term mitigations: revert, throttle, increase TTL, prompthash fallback.
- long-term fixes: add tokenizer-version pinning for prefix keys, migration tool to rehash prefixes on tokenizer upgrade, unit/e2e test for batching x tokenizer compatibility, observability alert for prefix churn anomaly.

maria (sre): assigning postmortem owner: prateek. I'll create an incident ticket and link customers.

dan (customer-ops): I'll follow up with customer postmortem notes to acme-payments and travelbuddy.

alyssa (oncall): handing off to morning oncall @maria for continued monitoring and postmortem writeup. my oncall shift notes: all mitigations applied, monitoring stable, watchlist created for next 24h for prefix churn and KV evictions.

maria (sre): taking handoff. thanks @alyssa. I'll schedule a 1hr sync with eng-runtime and platform tomorrow to plan migration and test coverage.

ops-bridge-bot: incident P1 resolved -> status: mitigated. Incident channel will remain open for follow-ups.

prateek (eng-runtime): quick debug snippet for postmortem: `grep -R "token_map_mismatch" /var/log/runtime/* | awk '{print $1, $5}' | sort | uniq -c` — helps find hot pods and time ranges.

alyssa (oncall): adding links to dashboards and logs to the incident ticket. closing my watch; handoff complete. :white_check_mark:

dan (customer-ops): will coordinate customer comms and share timelines for a root-cause summary.

maria (sre): noted. final note: create follow-up story to add an automated rollout guard that prevents simultaneous tokenizer and batching config changes in the same window.

prateek (eng-runtime): acknowledged, will draft the RFC for tokenizer compatibility and rollout gating.

incident-bot: Incident P1 mitigated at 2734568025.
